memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him. Then he commanded him: 'Do not marry a Canaanite woman. Go at once to Paddan Aram, to the house of your mother's father Bethuel. Take a wife for yourself there, from among the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.'" - Gen 28:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now Isaac blesses Jacob openly and knowingly — no disguise, no deception this time. And he gives him a clear command: do not marry a Canaanite woman, but go to the family in Paddan Aram and find a wife there. Isaac wanted Jacob to marry within the family of faith, among people who knew the true God.

Behind this instruction lies a concern for Jacob's spiritual future. Isaac had watched Esau marry Hittite women whose ways led away from God, and it had brought grief (Gen 26:34-35). He did not want the same for Jacob. The people we bind our lives to shape the direction of our hearts.

There is wisdom here for us. Our closest relationships — especially marriage — are among the most powerful influences on our walk with God. Scripture gently urges believers to seek partners who share their deepest faith (2 Cor 6:14), not out of pride, but because a shared love for God gives a home its firmest foundation.

Notice also that Jacob is sent out not aimlessly but with purpose. Even as he flees Esau's anger, God is directing his steps toward a family, a wife, and a future. What looked like mere escape was also God's leading. God can guide our path even through our hardest departures.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who are the closest influences shaping the direction of my heart?
2. Do I value shared faith in my most important relationships?
3. Can I trust that God is directing my steps even in hard seasons?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to choose my closest relationships wisely, treasuring a shared love for You. Thank You that You direct my steps even when I feel I am only running. Amen.
